[Beszel](https://beszel.dev) is a lightweight server monitoring tool: a small
agent on each machine reports to a **hub**, which keeps the history, shows the
dashboard and raises alerts. This integration reads your Beszel hub and brings
your systems into Gladys: one device per system, with whether it is online, its
CPU, memory, disk, highest temperature, network traffic, load, uptime, failed
services and the Beszel alerts triggered. Scenes can react when a system goes
offline or comes back, and when a Beszel alert is triggered or resolved; a
dashboard widget shows your systems at a glance. Everything stays on your local
network.

Tested against a real Beszel 0.21.0 hub and agent (Docker), with a system
stopped and started again and alerts triggered and resolved. Not yet on every
installation: feedback welcome on
[the issues](https://github.com/guim31/gladys-beszel/issues).

## What you need

- Gladys Assistant 5.1.0 or later.
- A Beszel hub (0.12 or later, 0.21 tested) reachable from the Gladys machine
  (port 8090 by default), with its agents already added.
- The email and password of a Beszel user. Best: a user created for Gladys,
  with the **read-only** role.

The integration only reads: it never changes anything in Beszel nor on your
machines.

## Getting started

### 1. Create a Beszel user for Gladys

The integration sees exactly what its user sees: the systems shared with it,
and **its own alerts**.

1. Open the admin panel of PocketBase, at `http://<hub>:8090/_/` (Beszel menu
   → **Users** in recent versions), and create a user in the `users`
   collection: an email, a password, the role `readonly`, `verified` ticked.
2. Share the systems with it: either start the hub with the environment
   variable `SHARE_ALL_SYSTEMS=true` (every user sees every system), or, in the
   same admin panel, add the user to the `users` field of each system.
3. Beszel alerts belong to a user: log into Beszel as this user and set the
   alerts the scenes should know (bell icon of a system). A read-only user may
   manage its own alerts.

You can also use your own Beszel account: the integration then sees your
systems and your alerts.

### 2. Configure the integration

In the **Configuration** tab of the integration:

- **Beszel address**: the address of the hub, as you open it in a browser:
  `192.168.1.20` (port 8090 added), `nas.lan:8090` or
  `https://beszel.example.com`.
- **Email of the Beszel user** and **Password**.
- **Refresh interval**: 30 seconds by default. The hub itself reads its agents
  once a minute: a shorter interval brings nothing.
- **Accept self-signed certificates**: only for an `https://` address whose
  certificate your browser does not trust either.
- **Language of the names**: language of the feature names, set when a device
  is added, and of the texts sent to scenes.

Save, then click **Test the connection**: it says the version of Beszel, how
many systems are online and how many alerts are triggered.

### 3. Add the systems

Open the **Discover** tab: every system of the user is listed. Add the ones you
want to follow. The scene triggers work for every system, added or not.

## The devices

Each system is one device, named as in Beszel. Its features:

- **Online**: 1 while Beszel marks the system up, 0 when it marks it down. A
  paused system sends nothing.
- **CPU**, **Memory** and **Disk**: the use, in %, of the processor, the
  memory and the root disk.
- **Highest temperature**: the temperature Beszel shows on its dashboard (the
  hottest sensor), in °C, when the system has sensors.
- **Network traffic**: sent and received together, in Mbit/s.
- **Load (1 min)**, **Load (5 min)**, **Load (15 min)**: the load averages.
- **Uptime**: in days.
- **Failed services**: the systemd services in failure, when the agent watches
  them.
- **Triggered alerts**: how many Beszel alerts of the user are triggered on
  this system.

The values that move all the time (CPU, memory, load, network, temperature)
are sent to Gladys at most once a minute, the others when they change. While
a system is down, only **Online** and **Triggered alerts** are updated: the
last figures stay.

## Dashboard

Add the **Beszel systems** widget to a dashboard:

- with no system chosen in its settings, it shows how many systems are online
  and offline and how many alerts are triggered, then one line per system, red
  when it is offline, orange with a triggered alert;
- with a system chosen, it shows its CPU, memory and disk gauges, its
  temperature, its triggered alerts, its load and its uptime.

The **Refresh** button reads Beszel again at once.

## Scenes

### Triggers

- **Beszel system offline or back**: Beszel marks a system down (its agent no
  longer answers) or up again. Filters: the system and the new state
  (**Offline**, **Back online**). The actions can use the system name and the
  new state. Beszel decides when a system is down; a paused system fires
  nothing.
- **Beszel alert**: a Beszel alert of the user is triggered or resolved.
  Filters: the system, the alert (**CPU**, **Memory**, **Disk**,
  **Temperature**, **Status**…) and the new state (**Triggered**,
  **Resolved**). The actions can use the system name, the alert, the alert
  with its threshold (`CPU > 80%`), the new state and the threshold.

The thresholds and durations of the alerts are set in Beszel, not in Gladys.
The states found when the integration starts are its starting point: only the
changes after that fire a scene, also across a restart of Gladys.

### Actions

- **State of a Beszel system**: reads a system and gives the next actions its
  figures (online, CPU, memory, disk, temperature, network, load, uptime,
  triggered alerts) and a ready-made summary, for example
  `nas: CPU 12%, memory 45%, disk 78%, 48 °C, no alert triggered`.
- **State of every Beszel system**: counts the systems online and offline and
  the triggered alerts, with a summary to send, for example
  `Offline: pi` then `nas: 1 alert(s) triggered (Disk > 90%)`.

### Scene ideas

- **Beszel system offline or back**, state **Offline** → send the message
  `{{triggerEvent.data.system_name}} is offline`.
- **Beszel alert**, alert **Temperature**, state **Triggered** → switch on the
  fan of the server room.
- Every morning at 8:00 → **State of every Beszel system** → send the summary.

## Troubleshooting

- **"does not answer"**: check the address and the port in a browser; a
  firewall may block port 8090.
- **"email or password refused"**: log into Beszel with them to check. A
  PocketBase superuser (the `/_/` admin account) is not a Beszel user: use an
  account of the `users` collection.
- **"Connected, but this Beszel user sees no system"**: share the systems with
  the user (step 1) or set `SHARE_ALL_SYSTEMS=true`.
- **No alert ever fires**: the alerts belong to the user the integration logs
  in with: set them in Beszel as this user.
- **"no Beszel hub at this address"**: another service answers there (another
  application, a reverse proxy without Beszel behind it).
- **No temperature**: the agent reads no sensor (a VM, or an agent in Docker
  without access to the sensors).
- More details with the `LOG_LEVEL=debug` environment variable on the
  integration.

## Limits

- One Beszel hub per installation, 100 systems at most.
- The summary of each system only: the containers, the extra disks, the GPU
  and the history of Beszel are not read.
- Only the alerts of the configured user are seen.
- Read every 30 seconds to 5 minutes, not in real time: the hub itself
  refreshes a system once a minute.
- Not affiliated with Beszel or its authors.

## Configuration settings

These are the settings Beszel asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Your Beszel hub | `section` | No | Enter the address of your Beszel hub and the email and password of a Beszel user: every system this user sees becomes a device. A read-only user is enough. Then add the systems you want from the Discover tab. |
| Beszel address | `string` | No | Address of the Beszel hub, the one of its web page (port 8090 by default): 192.168.1.20, nas.lan or https:\/\/beszel.example.com. |
| Email of the Beszel user | `string` | No | Best: a user created for Gladys, with the read-only role, with whom the systems are shared. |
| Password | `secret` | No | Kept by Gladys, sent only to the Beszel hub. |
| Options | `section` | No |  |
| Refresh interval | `select` | No | How often the Beszel hub is read. The hub itself refreshes each system once a minute. |
| Accept self-signed certificates | `boolean` | No | Only for an https:\/\/ address (Beszel behind a reverse proxy) whose certificate your browser does not trust either. |
| Language of the names | `select` | No | Language of the feature names (set when a device is added), of the scene results and of the connection test. |

## How to install Beszel in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: Beszel appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/guim31/gladys-beszel:1.0.1`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/guim31/gladys-beszel](https://github.com/guim31/gladys-beszel).

Beszel requires Gladys `>=5.1.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

Beszel is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core. It is published and maintained by [guim31](https://github.com/guim31), not by the Gladys core team.
